These fixtures use width-preserving synthetic text in place of freeform source content. cells-140.json and cells-168.json store each cell row as exact [glyph, colour_key, tint, count] runs; the oracle expands them and compares every cell and ordered hit array for every state. source.json points to view_model.json, which contains the same source values; long redacted strings use the fixture's transparent zlib/base85 encoding and test helpers decode them on load. The source_records.reference_literals table retains scrubbed reference-only literals that do not have a Fleet VM field; private strings, paths, and model identifiers are replaced before serialization.

PEERS cells and ordered hits are checked exactly against the approved reference at 140 and 168 columns, including the filtered f5 state. The independent renderer's hand-placed repository frames and link lanes are preserved as the oracle.

transitions.json is compact unindented JSON: cases store each viewer-main input chunk and a trace of state/frame references; shared frames intern identical frames, while the rows pool interns repeated cell rows stored as exact run-length records. Transition PEERS frames compare cells and ordered hits exactly with the same approved layout. Other transition frames compare all cells and ordered hits exactly.

Repository-only test runs compare the committed goldens. Running freeze_explorer.py --check with the external approved reference directory re-verifies provenance using the input hashes in manifest.json. The reference renderer and PNGs are intentionally external; no private absolute path is stored here. default-once.json is captured separately from the archived base CLI.

The `attempts` record carries the route it belongs to (`route`: f5). The reference draws one owner's raw output, on that route's page; the live builder names the route of the owner output the selection reader returned, so a route page never shows another route's lines.
